name: Blacksmith
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through active use — smelting, forging and finishing — unlocking forge stations, methods and higher tiers of metal, from bog iron to the skymetals and the legendary orange-gold horacalcum.
_thresholds_note: Copied from Herbalist deliberately, dip and all: the two tracks are meant to pace the same, a level-1 forge chain is worth about the same MP as a level-1 herb chain (3 first-time + 2 for a second stage), and a second curve would mean two clocks to balance instead of one. The dip at level 4 is the Herbalist author's and is deliberate — do not 'fix' it here either.
_deeds_note: Mirrors the Herbalist's legendary-catalyst lesson: the deed is the material, not the method, because polish is a level-5 method and gating level 5 on a level-5 method is a gate that never opens. A Blacksmith 4 reaches legendary metal the one way the rules allow below level 5: the novel-alloy rule, where alloying two different metals of the same tier yields a metal one band rarer — two exotic skymetals in one crucible is a legendary melt. rules/blacksmith.py implements that step.

legendary-metal.note: Any successful forging at legendary tier, however the metal was reached.

levels.note: Bar iron, horseshoes, plain blades and simple repairs.
Clean melts, fitted hafts and grips, silver and cold iron work.
True steel-making: crucible alloys and the heat-treatment that holds an edge.
Pattern-welding, wire-drawing and edge-work: the first masterwork pieces, and the skymetals.
Mirror finishes, legendary metal, and work that outlives its maker.

method_descriptions.smelt: Reduces ore to workable metal in the fire. Needs fuel in the charge, and metal above rare tier needs a fuel of rare tier or better — adamantine does not melt over charcoal.
method_descriptions.forge: Heats and hammers metal to shape on the anvil. The heart of every chain, and the step everything after the fire depends on. Needs fuel.
method_descriptions.quench: Plunges forged work into a bath to fix its hardness. What the bath is made of soaks into the steel — brine bites harder than water, and stranger liquids leave stranger marks.
method_descriptions.flux: Adds a cleansing agent to the melt that carries off slag and impurity. Strips the drawbacks of dirty ore the way Purify strips a poison — but it cleans the metal, not the smith: hazardous metal is hazardous still.
method_descriptions.rivet: Cold-joins fittings to finished metal: hafts, grips, guards and bindings. The way everything that is not the blade gets onto the blade.
method_descriptions.alloy: Melts two or more metals into one. Alloying two different metals of the same tier yields a metal one band rarer — a novel alloy is a discovery. Some metals refuse it: what makes cold iron cold iron does not survive the mixing.
method_descriptions.temper: Reheats quenched steel to a chosen colour and lets it down slowly, trading brittleness for spring. The step that separates a tool from a bar of hard iron, and the first requirement of fine and masterwork quality.
method_descriptions.draw: Pulls metal through a plate into wire and thin section — mail rings, springs, filigree. With fold, the shaping half of masterwork quality.
method_descriptions.fold: Doubles and welds the billet over itself, evening the carbon and layering the steel. The watered pattern on a fine blade is this method made visible.
method_descriptions.hone: Grinds and whets the working edge to its final geometry. With temper, what raises a piece from plain to fine.
method_descriptions.polish: Brings the surface to a mirror over days of ever-finer abrasive. The last touch on masterwork and the method of legendary metal.

_portable_note: The furnace and the masterwork forge are architecture, not baggage. Whether a chain can be attempted is therefore partly a question about where the character is standing, which is scene state rather than sheet state — same call as the Herbalist's still and workbench.
